newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile closes state-owned Lota coal mine.
newsitem.headline: Chile closes state-owned Lota coal mine.

text.p: The Chilean government ordered on Wednesday the closure of the loss-making state Lota coal mine in southern Chile, Mining Minister Benjamin Teplizky announced.
"The interior ministry has asked all the other ministries to cooperate to find a global solution to the problem of Lota," Teplizky said after announcing the decision.
"This final closure will be an opportunity for Lota as this production is definitely not profitable."
The pit is owned by state company Empresa Nacional del Carbon. The company was paralyzed for two months last year by a strike over job cuts.
The government will organize a programme to help the 1,100 workers who will lose their jobs find other work, he said.
The Lota mine, which lies at the heart of Chile's declining coal industry, is located in the Southern Bio Bio region, one of the country's poorest areas with very high unemployment.
